supporting_observations.claim: The large outbound transfer appears in the records at 13:50:19 UTC, rather than at approximately 13:46 UTC: the proxy records a CONNECT to ingest.ironvault-cloud.com with 640,000,000 client bytes, and Zeek records 640,000,212 origin bytes.

Immediately before the transfer, Ironvault's agent.exe ran on FILE-COP-01 as COPPERLINE\svc-backup with a Nightly job targeting ingest.ironvault-cloud.com; the network event is attributed to that process.
The destination, agent, service account, and transfer size match the supplied inventory description of approved Ironvault offsite backup, which uploads several hundred MB.

known_telemetry_limitations: The transfer is recorded as a proxy CONNECT tunnel; the available records establish the destination and byte count but do not expose the uploaded content. [T130-00259, T130-00260]
Collection-status metadata reports that winsec and Sysmon data for WS-SALI-01 were not collected from 13:30 to 14:00 UTC. This does not directly identify the FILE-COP-01 transfer.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish which files or data were uploaded in the Ironvault transfer. [T130-00259, T130-00260]
The records do not independently establish whether the Nightly backup was scheduled to run at 13:50 UTC; they do show the approved agent and target in the observed run. [T130-00257, T130-00258]
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: an unlisted Veeam Backup service started on FILE-COP-01, and that process later attempted to use svc-backup credentials to the proxy. This is outside the alerted Ironvault transfer. [T130-00402, T130-00416]

Separate ticket: FILE-COP-01 made proxy requests whose user agents identify GlobalProtect, Zscaler Client Connector, and python-requests to www.bing.com. These are not approved in the supplied inventory; the proxy records alone do not establish that a VPN session occurred or identify the process responsible for every request. [T130-00423, T130-00425, T130-00426]
